title: The Stone Sediment Threshold

features.name: the stone becoming sand
features.desc-on-touch: Here the boundary: on one side, stone that does not grow. On the other, sediment that remembers being stone and is learning to be water. The threshold is a question without an answer—not yet sand, not quite stone. This is where patience becomes visible.

features.name: the layer of recognition
features.desc-on-touch: A thin seam where sediment touches stone directly. The archive stored a memory here: a moment when the stone chamber understood it was not unchanging, but changing at a scale that felt like forever. The layer is the archive's recognition of that moment.

features.name: the grain that remembers weight
features.desc-on-touch: A single grain of sand that still remembers being stone. It carries the weight of the mountain in its crystalline memory. When you hold it, you feel the ridge that birthed it, the compression, the slow wearing down. The sediment is telling the story of stone learning to let go.

features.name: the flowing stillness
features.desc-on-touch: Water moves slowly through the threshold, so slowly you can only see its movement by memory. Yesterday the water was here. Today it is one grain farther down. The sediment flows without rushing. Patience is another form of water.

inscription: the threshold is not a place of ending but of learning a new form of slowness; nothing grows here but everything changes, grain by grain, memory by memory

reverie.title: REVERIE — when stone learned to speak through sediment
narr: You knelt in the dust between the stone face and its own
becoming. Katita held a grain up to the light, studying it.
She said: "It remembers the mountain." You could see it in her
eyes—not the grain, but the weight it carried forward, the
ancient pressure still singing in the crystalline lattice. She
was learning the language stones use to teach about dissolution.
